name: Acrobat
description:
The gap is wide, but you've got to make it anyway. You run forward, spacing your steps carefully - one, two, three - anchor your pole against the lip of the roof, tighten your grip and spring upward, propelled high over the busy alleyway below. As you complete an elegant arc downward you see the captain turn, noticing you, but too late. Using the momentum of your fall, you bring your pole down squarely on the crown of his helmet with a satisfying clang. He goes down. His guards wheel around to come to his defense, but you use the rebound of the initial blow to your advantage, bringing your pole down and around you in a wide sweep, knocking the legs out from under all three of them. You leap over the tangle of bodies and make a beeline for the doorway that leads down into the mansion. By the time the guards manage to get back to their feet, you're already gone.

Acrobats can run further, jump higher, climb faster and get to more places than anyone else. They aren't the hardest hitters on the battlefield, but they are incredibly difficult to pin down, leaping into and out of melee range before their opponents can react, striking from a distance with unusual weapons, or disabling a foe with carefully placed strikes.

The Acrobat mestiere uses Speed as a resource. With the Nimble ability, you are granted an exceptional range of movement, but you may choose to exchange that movement incrementally for actions, unleashing a surprisingly fierce barrage of attacks when you need to. This flexibility is the core of the Acrobat discipline, but you will also learn up to four additional special fighting techniques, specializing in the acrobat's pole, rope & chain weapons, shuriken and/or pressure point attacks. You will not be well-armored, so careful and quick movement is your first line of defense.

The Acrobat mestiere is among the most concise and focused. It gives you a lot of tactical options with a small number of abilities, gives you training in only a few types of weapons, and sidesteps the MP system entirely.

Play an Acrobat if you want to:

  • Go where no one else can, scaling, vaulting, and threading through environments with an ease that makes the impossible look routine.

  • Use movement itself as a resource, converting your speed into actions, attacks, and advantages that others simply cannot replicate.

  • Fight with unconventional weapons and techniques, from a long pole to chain weapons to precisely targeted strikes that disable a foe's body piece by piece.

Questions to consider when making an Acrobat:

  • Where did they train? A traveling circus, a martial arts tradition, a life spent free-running across urban rooftops, or some other experience?

  • What weapon—or fighting style—feels most like an extension of who they are? Is there a philosophy behind the choice, or is it purely practical?

  • How do they feel about their own physical capability? Is it a source of pride and identity, or simply a tool they use without much reflection?

  • Are they a performer as well as a fighter? Does everyone know what they can do, or do they keep it in reserve?

  • What is a place they have reached that no one thought reachable—and what did they find there?

novizio.description: You have developed your speed and agility to a level that sets you apart. You have at least some limited experience defending yourself, and have received basic training in one special fighting technique.
novizio.baseMpNotes: Acrobat abilities to not have an MP cost.
novizio.abilities: Nimble and choose one, ignoring its XP cost: Pole Training, Rope & Chain Weapon Training, Shuriken Training, or Pressure Point Training. Unless you chose Pressure Point Training, choose and gain one weapon appropriate to your training from this mestiere or from one of your home cultures.
novizio.gratuiti: Clothes and footwear that are easy to move in, a spool of wrist wrap, a small pouch of chalk.
